title: Launch scale and the SpaceX effect
question: How much launch capacity exists today, how fast is it growing, and how much of it is SpaceX?

headline.text: In 2025, SpaceX flew 51.7% of the world's 329 orbital launch attempts and carried 85.0% of the 4,570 payloads that reached orbit.

compute.where: MIT Engaging (final run, job 26814679) and local Mac (development); stdlib Python, identical GCAT files by SHA-256

jobs.name: of-logistics-gcat
jobs.note: final run with the committed script

method: Download the GCAT launch list (launch.tsv), the derived per-payload orbital launch log (launchlog.tsv) and all object catalogs (satcat*, auxcat, lprcat, tmpcat, csocat).
Orbital launch attempt = LaunchCode starting O (orbital) or D (deep space) with second letter S (success) or F (failure); OE (failed before ignition) and OA (aborted, no launch) are excluded.
SpaceX = launch agency SPX in GCAT (who flew the rocket, not who owns the payload).
Payloads per year = launchlog rows on successful orbital/deep-space launches; Starlink = name or payload name starting "Starlink".

Mass to orbit = sum of the GCAT Mass column (payload launch mass, kg) joined by JCAT from the object catalogs; coverage = share of payloads with a positive mass. The GCAT OrbPay column (autogenerated, flagged by GCAT as "use with caution") is kept only as a cross-check in the table.
Rideshare = launches whose flight or mission name matches Transporter-N or Bandwagon-N; payloads per mission = launchlog payload rows with that launch designation.
Starship = every launch of LV_Type Starship*; integrated flights are those not coded A (atmospheric hop).

charts.title: Orbital launch attempts per year
charts.subtitle: SpaceX versus everyone else, 2000 to date (2026 YTD = to 2026-10-24)
charts.caption: GCAT launch list, LaunchCode O* or D* (orbital and deep-space attempts, successes and failures). Shows launch counts by launch provider (GCAT Agency = SPX), not who owns the payloads.

charts.title: Payloads placed in orbit per year
charts.subtitle: Starlink, other SpaceX-launched payloads, and payloads launched by others (2026 YTD = to 2026-10-24)
charts.caption: GCAT derived launchlog (one row per payload). Counts payloads, not mass; most are small satellites. Payloads lost on failed launches are excluded (they are listed in the stats).

charts.title: Payload mass placed in orbit per year
charts.subtitle: Sum of GCAT payload launch masses, 1957–2025 (complete years only)
charts.caption: Sums the Mass column of every payload with a mass value (100.0% of 2025 payloads have one). Many masses are GCAT estimates (flagged ?), and secret payloads are often nominal. Upper stages are excluded.

charts.title: Payloads per SpaceX rideshare mission
charts.subtitle: Transporter and Bandwagon missions, catalogued payloads per launch
charts.caption: Counts GCAT payload entries sharing the mission's launch designation. Includes payloads released later by orbital transfer vehicles; the newest missions may still be incompletely catalogued.

charts.title: Starship integrated flights
charts.subtitle: Apogee of each integrated flight; GCAT codes flights 4 onward as orbital (target perigee > 0)
charts.caption: All integrated Starship/Super Heavy flights in the GCAT launch list. Apogee only. GCAT notes some orbital codings are borderline. Payloads catalogued per flight (in stats) include the ship itself and Starlink mass simulators.

findings: GCAT lists 7,414 orbital launch attempts from 1957 to 2026-10-24; 2025 had 329, 3.78x the 87 of 2015.
SpaceX flew 170 of the 329 orbital launch attempts in 2025 (51.7%).
4,570 payloads reached orbit in 2025; 85.0% rode SpaceX rockets and 3,193 were Starlink.
Catalogued payload mass placed in orbit in 2025 sums to 3,096.4 t (84.8% on SpaceX launches), 10.28x the 301.1 t of 2015; 100.0% of 2025 payloads have a mass in GCAT.
Through Oct 24: 252 orbital attempts in 2026 (122 by SpaceX) vs 250 (139 by SpaceX) in the same window of 2025: growth has paused this year in GCAT's count.
23 Transporter/Bandwagon rideshare missions carried 1,742 catalogued payloads (median 74 per mission, range 4–145).

Starship has made 14 integrated flights (10 coded successful by GCAT). GCAT puts 11 of them (flight 4 onward, including two failures) in its orbital category (target perigee above zero within uncertainties); the successful ones have GCAT perigees of -40 to 8 km, i.e. at the edge of orbit.
limitations: 2026 is partial (data to 2026-10-24); year-to-date comparisons use the same calendar window.
Launch counts follow GCAT definitions (McDowell); other trackers differ by a few launches a year on borderline cases (Starship, failures before orbit).

Mass sums use payload launch masses, many of which are GCAT estimates (flagged ?), and classified payloads with nominal masses. They exclude upper stages, so they understate total mass to orbit. Coverage per year is reported.
SpaceX share counts the launch provider. Payload owners differ: Starlink is SpaceX-owned, while rideshare payloads belong to hundreds of organisations.
Recent rideshare missions may not be fully catalogued yet, so their payload counts are lower bounds.
This is capacity *up*. A foundry also needs capacity *down*, which is far scarcer: see return-cadence.json.
future_big_data: Join Space-Track TLE histories (all payloads, ~10^8 element sets) to measure orbit-raising and lifetime by operator, to size free-flyer foundry orbits.
Add per-launch price data (public FAA/press filings) to compute $/kg trends next to the mass series.
Track Starship payload deployments once they are catalogued, to calibrate a heavy-lift foundry delivery scenario.

partners.name: SpaceX
partners.why: Flies most of the world's launches and rideshare slots; Transporter/Bandwagon is the cheapest route to orbit for a first foundry cartridge.
partners.evidence: 51.7% of 2025 orbital attempts and 85.0% of 2025 payloads in GCAT; 23 rideshare missions with 1,742 payloads.

partners.name: Rocket Lab
partners.why: Second most frequent US launcher, and it built the spacecraft buses for Varda's W-series capsules.
partners.evidence: GCAT launch agency RLABN flew 17 orbital attempts in 2025 (rank 4 by launch agency); GCAT lists Rocket Lab (RLABLB) as manufacturer of the Varda W-1, W-2, W-3 spacecraft; later W-series buses are Varda-built.

partners.name: Jonathan McDowell (GCAT)
partners.why: Maintains the open catalog every number here comes from.
partners.evidence: All launch, payload and mass counts in this file are computed from GCAT TSVs (Updated 2026 Oct 24 1902:29).
